item.name: Audit
item.description: Score one page or several: 80+ checks, a 0 to 100 score, a grade and a prioritized fix list.

description.content:
Run a comprehensive SEO audit on any URL.

Returns an overall score (0–100), letter grade, prioritized fix
recommendations, and a `audit` block of category breakdowns
(SEO, performance, accessibility, AI readability).

Paid plans (Starter $5/mo and up) additionally receive:
  - `sxo`, `aeo`, `aio` — extended scoring blocks
  - `history` — delta vs the previous audit for this URL
    (overall score, grade change, per-category deltas, days since)
  - Full priorities list and uncapped per-category checks

Every priority carries `plain_english` (one jargon-free sentence) and
`who_fixes_it` (`developer` | `content` | `marketing`) next to `issue`/`fix`.

`?include=trackers` (paid plans) adds a `trackers` block: the same inventory as
`GET /trackers`, at no extra audit. It adds a few seconds.

`?include=conversion` (paid plans) adds a `conversion` block: the same score and
fix list as `GET /conversion`, at no extra audit. Combine them: `?include=trackers,conversion`.

Free / demo keys see gated placeholders for the paid blocks
(`_extended_gated`, `history._gated`, `_priorities_gated`).

**Core Web Vitals are opt-in: `?cwv=true`** (every plan, no extra charge, never
part of the score). The response always carries a `core_web_vitals` object with
`lcp_ms`, `inp_ms`, `cls`, `fcp_ms`, `ttfb_ms`, `checks` and a `status`:

  - `not_requested` (the default): no measurement was made; the metrics are
    `null` and `hint` says how to ask. A default audit never waits on PageSpeed.
  - `ok`: measured by Google PageSpeed Insights. `source` is `field` (real-user
    Chrome UX Report data) or `lab`; `_cached: true` when it came from the
    24 hour cache. A cached measurement is included even without `cwv=true`,
    because it costs no time.
  - `unavailable`: `cwv=true` was set but PageSpeed failed, rate limited us or
    was too slow; `reason` says which. The audit itself still succeeds.
  - `unavailable` with `pending: true`: PageSpeed was still measuring when the
    wait ran out (about 25 seconds). The measurement finishes in the
    background; the next audit of that URL has it.

With `cwv=true` the first audit of a URL takes about 10 seconds longer; repeats
within 24 hours are instant. Set your client timeout to 60 seconds.

Requires an API key passed in the `X-API-Key` header.
(Required) The URL to audit (e.g., https://example.com)
Comma-separated extras on paid plans: `trackers` (tracker and pixel inventory) and `conversion` (conversion score). Each adds a few seconds.

Add `"cwv": true` to the body to include measured Core Web Vitals for every
URL (see `GET /audit` for the `core_web_vitals` statuses). It is off by default:
each result then says `status: "not_requested"`, or carries a measurement that
was already cached. With it on, the measurements run side by side while the
URLs are audited, and the batch as a whole waits at most about 50 seconds on
them; a URL whose measurement is not ready reads `unavailable` + `pending: true`
and has it on the next audit. Set your client timeout to 180 seconds.

item.name: Accessibility
item.description: Automated WCAG 2.1 A/AA checks. Automated testing does not catch everything.

description.content:
Run an ADA / WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility compliance audit. Paid plans only.

Returns a detailed accessibility report including:
- Overall compliance score and grade (WCAG 2.1 A/AA rules only)
- Lawsuit risk assessment (high/medium/low/minimal)
- Category breakdowns (images, forms, contrast, keyboard, ARIA, etc.)
- `violations`: WCAG 2.1 AA failures, with affected elements and a plain-English fix
- `best_practices`: axe best-practice findings (e.g. heading-order). Not WCAG
  requirements, so they never lower the score or raise the risk level
- `needs_review`: checks axe couldn't decide automatically, with what to verify by hand.
  They are excluded from the score rather than counted as failures
- `priorities`: WCAG violations first, then best practices. `severity` maps from axe
  `impact` one-to-one: critical→critical, serious→high, moderate→medium, minor→low
  (best practices are always low)

**Limits.** ADA audits have their own monthly allowance (`ada_monthly`: Starter 5,
Basic 20, Pro 100, Ultra 500), separate from your audit quota. Each key may run
20 ADA audits per minute and 2 at a time; the tier `rpm` does not apply here.
`GET /usage` reports `ada_usage_this_month` and `ada_remaining`.
A 429 includes `Retry-After`, and a 429 is never counted against `ada_monthly`
(nor is any failed audit).

**Errors.** A page we can't load returns **422** with `detail` (message) and
`reason`: `blocked` (the site refused our crawler), `timeout`, `dns`, `tls`,
`unreachable`, `not_found`, `http_error`, `non_html`, `redirect_loop`,
`blocked_url`, `load_failed`. A URL we refuse up front (private/internal address,
malformed URL) is **400** with `reason` `blocked_url` / `invalid_url`. A **502**
means the failure was on our side.

Uses the axe-core accessibility engine (industry standard) to check
against WCAG 2.1 Level AA — the standard referenced in most ADA lawsuits.
(Required) The URL to audit for ADA/WCAG compliance
`trackers` adds the tracker and pixel inventory to the report

item.name: Page analysis
item.description: Trackers, conversion, Search Console quick wins and backlinks.

item.name: Tracking pixels and tags on a page

request.name: Tracking pixels and tags on a page

description.content:
List the third-party trackers and pixels a page loads.

Loads the page in a real browser, waits a few seconds, and reports every analytics,
advertising, session-replay, chat, marketing-automation, A/B-testing and monitoring
tool it saw, including pixels a tag manager injects (which never appear in the page
source).

Each item in `trackers` has `vendor`, `category`, `found_in` (`html`, `network`),
`injected` (seen on the network but not in the source), `requests`,
`transfer_bytes`, `evidence` (up to 3 URLs) and, where one is exposed, `ids`
(a GA4, GTM or Google Ads id). `summary` totals them by category and names the
`consent_manager` on the page, if any.

This lists what loaded during one visit with no interaction. It does not determine
whether a tracker waited for consent, and it is not legal advice.

Counts as one audit against your plan. A page we can't load returns **422** with
`reason`, and is not counted.
(Required) The page to inspect (e.g., https://example.com)

Score how well a page turns a visitor into a lead or a sale.

Reads the page's HTML (the same fetch `/audit` uses: plain HTTP, then a real browser
when the page is built by JavaScript) and scores five areas from 0 to 100:

- `headline`: one H1 that says what the page offers, with a sentence under it
- `cta`: a call to action near the top, worded as an action, repeated down the page.
  A phone link and "Add to cart" both count
- `trust`: testimonials, ratings, guarantees, contact details, credentials
- `forms`: how many fields the form asks for, and whether they are labeled
- `objections`: price or a path to it, FAQ, what happens next, shipping and returns

Returns `score`, `grade`, `page_type`, `categories` (per-area score, weight and
checks), `signals` (what we found: the H1, the button labels, the trust evidence)
and `priorities`, the fix list. Every priority has `severity`, `category`, `issue`,
`fix`, `plain_english` and `who_fixes_it` (`developer` | `content` | `marketing`),
plus `evidence` where there is some.

**What it does not do.** It does not measure your conversion rate; only your
analytics can. "Near the top" is source order, not pixels: we do not lay the page
out. A form embedded from another service (HubSpot, Calendly, Typeform) is reported
but not scored, and a page with no form is not marked down for it: `forms.score`
is `null` and its weight goes to the other areas. A page over 3 MB is scored on what
we read, and nothing is reported as missing.

Counts as one audit against your plan. A page we can't load or can't read returns
**422** with `reason` and is not counted. Free keys get the scores and the first
two priorities; paid plans get the full list. `?include=conversion` on `/audit`
(paid plans) adds the same block to an audit at no extra charge.
(Required) The page to score (e.g., https://example.com/services)
`local_service`, `ecommerce`, `saas` or `general`. Detected from the page when omitted.

item.name: Page-two quick wins from your Search Console rows

request.name: Page-two quick wins from your Search Console rows

description.content:
Find the page-2 quick wins in your Search Console data.

Send your own Search Console rows and get back the queries ranking 11-20 that are
worth working on first, each with the page it lands on, an opportunity score and an
estimate of the extra clicks from moving it onto page 1.

**We do not connect to your Search Console.** You export the rows (Performance
report CSV, or the Search Analytics API with the `query` and `page` dimensions)
and send them. Nothing is fetched and nothing is stored.

Send JSON with either `rows` or `csv`:

- `rows`: `[{"query": "...", "page": "https://...", "clicks": 3, "impressions": 900, "position": 11.4}]`.
  The API's own shape (`{"keys": ["query", "page"], "clicks": ...}`) works too. `page` is optional.
- `csv`: the export as text, with a header row. Column names are matched
  (`Top queries`/`Query`, `Page`, `Clicks`, `Impressions`, `Position`).
- `min_impressions` (default 50), `target_position` (1-10, default 5), `limit` (default 25, max 200)
- `exclude_terms`: words to leave out, such as your brand name
- `ctr_curve`: your own expected click-through rate by position, `{"1": 0.28, "2": 0.15}`

Each item in `quick_wins` has `query`, `page`, `position`, `impressions`, `clicks`,
`ctr`, `expected_ctr`, `opportunity_score` (0-100: 40% how close to page 1, 40%
impressions, 20% how far clicks fall short of expected), `estimated_extra_clicks`
at the target position with a range (position 10 to position 3), an `action`
(`small_push`, `improve_page`, `fix_snippet`, `consolidate`) and a `plain_english`
sentence. `also_ranking_pages` lists other pages of yours showing for the same query.
`pages` groups the wins by landing page.

**Read the numbers as estimates.** Google publishes no click-through curve; the
default is a rough one. Extra clicks hold impressions constant and assume every
impression is a person. Position is an average over the export's dates, countries
and devices.

**Send the whole export, not only page 2.** With 500 or more page-1 impressions in
the rows, `ctr_calibration` compares the clicks your page-1 results earned with
what the curve predicts (`ratio`), and each win also gets
`estimated_extra_clicks_calibrated` (the estimate times that ratio). A ratio far
below 1 usually means many of the impressions are rank trackers or bots.

Works on every plan. Counts as one audit; a request we reject (400) is not counted.
Up to 1 MB of JSON per request (roughly 5,000 rows with URLs); filter the export
to positions 11-20 first if yours is larger.

Return observed backlinks for a target domain.

Audit-fed dataset: every audit run by SEO Score API customers contributes
observations. Not a comprehensive backlink index — see `data_caveat` in the
response. Requires Basic plan ($15/mo) or higher.
(Required) Target domain (e.g. example.com)
Max sample rows to return

item.name: Site crawl
item.description: Crawl a site and score its pages (asynchronous).

description.content:
Start a multi-page crawl of one site (async).

Follows same-site links from `url`, plus the URLs in the sitemap, up to your page cap,
and reports broken pages, redirects, duplicate titles and headings, pages missing a
title or heading, orphan pages (in the sitemap, linked from nowhere crawled) and slow
pages. Plain HTTP requests, 4 at a time, robots.txt honoured.

**Limits.** Pro: 25 pages per crawl, 20 crawls a month. Ultra: 100 pages, 100 crawls a
month. Any other plan: one Deep Audit credit covers a 25-page crawl. A failed crawl is
not counted and a credit is returned.

Returns `job_id`; poll `GET /crawl/{job_id}`. `site_map` is a shareable page with the
site diagram once the crawl has finished.

Poll a site crawl. `status` is `queued`, `running`, `completed` or `failed`.

While running, `pages_done` counts up. When completed, `result` holds `summary`,
`issues` (broken_links, redirects, duplicate_titles, duplicate_h1, missing_title,
missing_h1, orphan_pages, slow_pages, noindex_pages, rate_limited), `pages` (one row
per URL: status, depth, redirects, response_ms, title, h1, canonical, inlinks) and
`links` (the internal link graph). Only the key that started a crawl can read it.
(Required)

item.name: Deep Site Audit
item.description: Asynchronous audit from a catalog of 14,000+ checks.

description.content:
Queue a Deep Site Audit of one URL and get a `job_id` back immediately.

The audit fetches the page and its supporting signals (robots.txt, sitemap,
DNS, TLS, PageSpeed), runs the thousands of catalog checks that apply to it, then an AI analysis pass of up to 150 checks. It takes
about 90 seconds once it starts, so poll `GET /site-audit/{job_id}`.

**Included on Pro (20/month) and Ultra (100/month).** Any other key spends one
purchased Deep Audit credit per audit. A failed audit gives its quota unit or
credit back.

item.name: AI Citations
item.description: Track whether AI assistants mention and cite your brand.

description.content:
Track a brand's visibility in AI answers. Requires Starter ($5/mo) or higher.

Send JSON: {"brand": "Acme", "domains": ["acme.com"], "prompts": ["best CRM for agencies"],
"competitors": ["Rival"], "engines": ["chatgpt","gemini","perplexity","claude"],
"samples": 3, "cadence": "weekly", "webhook_url": "https://..."}

**No prompts yet?** Leave `prompts` out and send `"starter": {"topic": "CRM",
"audience": "agencies"}` instead. The tracker is created with a starter set built
from `topic`, your `brand` and `competitors` (the same list
`GET /citations/prompts/starter` returns), cut to the tracked prompts your plan has
left and to what one run can spend of your monthly checks at the tracker's engines
and samples. With no `cadence`, a starter tracker runs weekly when the allowance
covers a month of weekly runs, otherwise monthly. The response's `starter` block
says how many were generated and kept, the checks per run and the cadence chosen.
Edit them later with `PATCH`.

Monthly allowance (checks / tracked prompts): Starter 150 / 15, Basic 500 / 30,
Pro 1,500 / 75, Ultra 4,000 / 200. A check is one prompt on one engine, sampled once.

List this key's citation trackers.

`usage` reports the month and any top-up: `checks_limit`, `checks_used` and
`checks_remaining` are the plan's monthly allowance; `topup_checks_remaining` is the
purchased balance (spent only after the month's checks, never reset, expires 12 months
after purchase: `topup_next_expiry`); `checks_available` is what a run can spend now.
The same block is on `GET /usage` as `citations`.
Read one tracker.
(Required)
Edit a tracker's prompts, engines, competitors, samples, cadence or webhook.
(Required)
Stop tracking a brand. Run history is kept until its retention expires.
(Required)

Run a tracker now. Every prompt × engine × sample counts as one check.

A run needs all of its checks up front: the month's remaining allowance plus any
top-up balance. If that is short the run is refused with 429 and nothing is spent.
Buy more with `POST /citations/topups/checkout`. A check whose engine returned an
error is not counted against either balance.

A run that finishes within 45 seconds returns its summary (200). A longer one returns
**202** with `run_id`, `status: "running"` and `poll`; it keeps running, and
`GET /citations/runs/{run_id}` reports `completed` with the results when it is done.
(Required)
Run status plus every per-prompt, per-engine result.
(Required)
Timeseries of mention rate, citation rate, share of voice and average position.
(Required)

Top-up packs for AI citation checks, and this account's balance.

A top-up is a one-time purchase for when the month's checks run out: 500 checks for
$10 or 2,000 for $36 (`packs` is the live list). Top-up checks are spent only after
the plan's monthly allowance, do not reset on the 1st, and expire 12 months after
purchase. `can_buy` is false on the free tier, which cannot run citation checks.

Auto-reload setting for AI citation checks, and this month's use.

Read-only. Auto-reload is **off unless you turn it on, and it can only be turned on
or changed from the dashboard** (signed in), never with an API key, because turning it
on authorizes charges. When on, a run that needs more checks than you have is not
refused: we charge the card on your subscription for one pack (`pack`: "500" = $10,
"2000" = $36), add the checks and let the run go ahead, every time you run out.
`reloads_this_month`, `charged_this_month_usd` and `failed_this_month` show what has
happened so far; after 2 failed charges in a row it pauses (`paused`) until you save
the setting on the dashboard again.

A starter set of prompts to track, from your topic, brand, competitors and audience.

Covers the six kinds of question buyers ask an AI assistant: `direct_recommendation`,
`comparison`, `alternatives`, `feature_specific`, `use_case` and `pricing`. Built from
fixed templates, not a model: the same inputs always return the same list, nothing is
fetched, and no AI check is spent. A template that needs an input you didn't send is
left out, so with no `competitors` the comparison prompts are generic.

`prompts` is the flat list, interleaved across categories, ready to send as `prompts`
to `POST /citations/trackers`. `categories` groups them; `items` flags which ones name
your brand or a competitor.

The default is two per category, 12 prompts. Run on the default four engines at three
samples that is 144 checks, which fits one run a month on Starter (150 checks).

Works on every plan and is not metered. Treat the list as a first draft: rewrite it in
the words your buyers use. To read prompts off a website instead, use
`GET /citations/prompts/suggest`.

SEO Score API audits a web page and returns JSON: a 0 to 100 score, a grade, category scores, AI readability scores and a prioritized fix list.

**Setup:** get a free key (20 audits a month, no credit card) at https://seoscoreapi.com/#signup, or run *Account > Request a free API key* and then *Verify the emailed code*.
